{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** Our table built a fish: a rounded body, a forked tail and a nose lead-in. All 113 standing dominoes connect to the start and should fall, so I expect the judge to read it as a fish. My part was the bottom body line, which I laid from the nose to about halfway. Maya carried it out to the lower tip. So I contributed a solid share of the outline, but I wasn't the one who finished it. I also didn't add detail like an eye, which was on the pad as a label but never built. The picture works, but I didn't push it beyond the basics.

**Execution:** I laid my section of the bottom line cleanly. It left one small stray domino pointing up, and Priya spotted it. I said it was gone, but looking at the table now, a small stub still sits near the middle of the bottom line. Priya judged it harmless and it doesn't break the chain, but my statement was inaccurate and I should have re-checked before saying so. After that I said I'd inspect the tail join, but Priya and Leo were already checking it, so I mostly watched. I could have used my free hands better in the last few minutes.

**Collaboration:** The team handed out jobs quickly, and I took the bottom line without fuss. I answered Priya's question about the stub and stayed out of Leo's way while he laid the back edge, so nobody bumped anyone. I also agreed with the hands-off call before the push. I was quiet through most of the middle stretch, and I could have spoken up sooner to say Maya's takeover freed me to help elsewhere.

**Leadership:** I didn't lead this one. Leo and Priya coordinated, and I followed. I was a reliable teammate, but I didn't propose improvements or take ownership of any open issue. Next time I'd offer to fix small problems like the stub rather than just reporting on them."}
